questions.q: Why does Average Order Value use DIVIDE instead of the / operator?
options: The / operator doesn't exist in DAX
DIVIDE returns a blank instead of an error when Order Count is zero, which matters once slicers can filter to nothing
DIVIDE is required syntax in every DAX measure
DIVIDE always rounds to two decimal places
questions.explain: DIVIDE handles the zero-denominator case gracefully, which a plain / would not.

questions.q: What does Prior Week Sales's CALCULATE + DATEADD combination actually do?
options: Re-evaluates Total Sales inside a filter context shifted back 7 days on the Date table
Filters out any order with a NULL ship date
Deletes the last 7 days of data from the model
Averages sales across the entire year
questions.explain: CALCULATE re-evaluates an expression inside a modified filter context, and DATEADD shifts the date filter back by the given interval.

questions.q: What does ALL ( TerritoryDim ) do inside the Total Sales (All Regions) measure?
options: Removes any filter currently applied through the TerritoryDim relationship, so the measure reflects every territory
Deletes the TerritoryDim table from the model
Sorts TerritoryDim alphabetically
Restricts the measure to only one territory
questions.explain: ALL strips away filters on the specified table, which is exactly what a company-wide benchmark figure needs.

questions.q: Why do Total Sales and Total Sales (All Regions) return the exact same number when no region filter is applied?
options: Power BI caches the first measure's result for the second
ALL has nothing to strip away when nothing is filtered in the first place
They are actually the same measure with two different names
They never return the same number under any condition
questions.explain: With no filter narrowing the territory, removing filters via ALL changes nothing, so both measures compute identically until a slicer is applied.

questions.q: What makes Avg Days to Ship a row-context calculation rather than a simple aggregation?
options: It is actually a plain column aggregation, not row-context
AVERAGEX computes the ship lag per row of Fact before averaging the results
It uses the SUM function internally
It filters on ShipDate only, with no row iteration
questions.explain: AVERAGEX iterates row by row, computing DATEDIFF per order line, then averages those per-row results.
